district.name: Ballari
district.description: Dominated by the massive monolithic Ballari Fort rock, Ballari features the lush green Krauncha Giri hills of Sandur, 7th-century Early Chalukyan Kumaraswamy Temple, and Asia's first Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary.
district.descriptionKannada: ಏಕಶಿಲಾ ಬಂಡೆಯ ಮೇಲಿನ ಬಳ್ಳಾರಿ ಕೋಟೆಯಿಂದ ಕಂಗೊಳಿಸುವ ಈ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆ, ಸಂಡೂರಿನ ಹಸಿರು ಕ್ರೌಂಚಗಿರಿ ಕಣಿವೆ, ೭ನೇ ಶತಮಾನದ ಕುಮಾರಸ್ವಾಮಿ ದೇವಾಲಯ ಮತ್ತು ದರೋಜಿ ಕರಡಿ ಧಾಮಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧ.

destinations.name: Ballari Fort (Upper & Lower)
destinations.description: Dominating the skyline from atop a massive 600-foot monolithic rock, the fort features two distinct levels: Upper Fort built by Hanumappa Nayaka with huge rainwater cisterns and Citadel, and Lower Fort fortified with French bastions by Hyder Ali.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Dating from the 16th century under Vijayanagara feudatories, captured and modernized in 1769 by Hyder Ali and later occupied by British garrison.
destinations.culturalImportance: A monumental sentinel over the plains; legendary engineer legend claims Hyder Ali hanged the French architect when he realized the opposite rock was higher.

photos.caption: Ballari Fort (Upper & Lower)
photos.source: Archaeological Survey of India & Karnataka State Gazetteer

destinations.bestSeason: October to March (Climb early morning or late afternoon)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Accessible by town roads; stone stairway to upper fort
destinations.safetyInstructions: Carry drinking water; steep stone steps can be hot during midday sun.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Protected by Archaeological Survey of India
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Archaeological Survey of India & Karnataka State Gazetteer

destinations.name: Kumaraswamy & Parvati Temples, Sandur
destinations.description: Nestled deep in the lush green Krauncha Giri hills of Sandur, this extraordinary dual temple complex comprises the 7th-century Early Chalukyan Parvati Temple and the 8th-century Rashtrakuta Kumaraswamy Temple amidst iron-ore forests.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Built by Badami Chalukyas (Parvati shrine) and Rashtrakutas (Kartikeya shrine); later patronized by the Ghorpade Maharajas of Sandur.
destinations.culturalImportance: Traditionally the Kumaraswamy shrine had historic restrictions that were reformed under Mahatma Gandhi's guidance during his 1934 temple-entry tour.
destinations.bestSeason: September to February (Mahatma Gandhi said 'See Sandur in September')
destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: 12 km from Sandur town, 45 km from Ballari
destinations.nearestRailwayStation: Toranagallu Junction (28 km) or Ballari (45 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Picturesque winding ghat road through Sandur hills
destinations.safetyInstructions: Winding forest roads; drive slowly around hill hairpins. Watch for wildlife crossings.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Protected under Archaeological Survey of India; active worship

destinations.name: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary
destinations.description: Asia's first dedicated sanctuary for Indian Sloth Bears, spanning 82 sq km of rugged bouldered hills, thorny scrub forest, and caves sheltering over 120 sloth bears, leopards, pangolins, and monitor lizards with a dedicated watchtower.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Established in 1994 to protect the indigenous sloth bear population that has inhabited Bilikallu rock formations since Ramayana times (legendary Jambavan).
destinations.culturalImportance: A triumph of dry-zone wildlife conservation where bears emerge daily in late afternoon to feed on rock face treats laid by forest staff.
destinations.bestSeason: October to March (Bear viewing optimal 15:30 to 18:00)
destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: 15 km from Hampi, 20 km from Hospet, 50 km from Ballari
destinations.roadAccessibility: Paved road via Kamalapur to Daroji entrance gate
destinations.safetyInstructions: Remain quiet in the watchtower. Do not feed wildlife. Vehicles restricted to designated tracks.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Forest Department entry ticket at gate
